purpose: Prevent analytical compression: narrative fact, visual extent, question, interpretation, source quote and character-specific behavior must never collapse into one vague event.

non_negotiable_rules.detail: raw/Dhika.txt read-only. All analysis sources are pointers to exact episode-local original lines.
Do not invent historical actions or change event timing. Hypotheses remain explicitly noncanonical until compared with the original.
A scene may contain dozens of discrete choices, gazes, touch gestures, reactions, description beats and dialogue turns. Count separately where materially distinct.
Keep actor intention, narrator assertions, each character's observation, stated belief, questions, and incorrect dialogue labels separate.
Questions about prior experience, descriptions of imagined acts, and overstatements by a speaker are not proof the questioned/described event happened.

If source establishes partial visibility, record observed part and substantial degree, preserving garment and narrator's full context; do not silently reduce the event to outfit change or expand it to complete disrobing.
Track per-character and per-relationship dialogue, repeated phrases, narrator access, pacing, gestures, reaction timing, knowledge gaps. Avoid universal/generic style claims.
Shared source window once; store Bantu, Bobby and Dhika reactions and spoken claims individually with line IDs.
Record last real action/question, where everyone is, whether scene actually ended, and whether next episode immediately resumes or uses flashback.
Freeze target episode prediction before reading its raw source; never edit its content after evaluating it; exact-action misses reported explicitly.
Separate machine-verification from editorial completeness. Passing tests is necessary but not sufficient.

case_study_e04.failure: Substantial partial visibility and conflicting topless terminology compressed away into clothing and generic dialogue labels
case_study_e04.canonical_interpretation: Substantial partial upper-body visibility is supported. A speaker's topless question/claim and Dhika's blouse-still-on correction are distinct source facts.

release_gates.machine: All pointers valid and consistent with raw; no duplicate IDs, impossible references or forecast/canon contamination
release_gates.editorial: Evidence-completeness audit per scene, especially unnamed actions, body description, intentions, multiple character viewpoints and narrator/character contrasts
release_gates.status_reporting: Claim fully reviewed only after both gates; never equate schema validation with accuracy or coverage.
